name: Great Ocean Road Tour and VIP Wildlife Experience
headings: Stop 1: Guaranteed Australian Wildlife Encounter – Only with Us -  中文版本在英文下方 Your day begins with something no other Great Ocean Road tour can offer — a guaranteed, hands-on encounter with real Australian wildlife, including koalas you can pat and photograph under licensed supervision. While other tours promise “wildlife spotting,” we guarantee it. No hoping for distant glimpses — this is a genuine, up-close experience in a private, weather-safe indoor venue at Akuna Anglesea, hosted by WildlifeXposure’s licensed wildlife educators. You’ll meet: Koalas – touch and take photos (supervised) Snakes, crocodiles, and native birds Possums, gliders, dragons and lizards This unforgettable VIP session includes morning tea at Akuna’s award-winning restaurant — coffee, pastries, paninis, and fresh juice — before we hit the road. Stop 2: Great Ocean Road Memorial Arch Next, we visit the famous Memorial Arch, the historic gateway built by returned WWI servicemen — the world’s largest war memorial. It’s a perfect photo stop and the true start of your coastal adventure. Stop 3: Apollo Bay – Seaside Lunch Relax in Apollo Bay, a charming coastal village where the Otways meet the sea. Enjoy free time for lunch, beach walks, or local shopping before continuing west. Stop 4: The Twelve Apostles – Coastal Icons We finish at the breathtaking Twelve Apostles, Victoria’s most photographed natural wonder. Walk the viewing boardwalks and capture unforgettable photos of the rugged cliffs and ocean stacks. Return Journey The return trip winds inland through the Otway forest and countryside, offering a peaceful end to your full-day adventure. No other tour gives you this — a guaranteed hands-on koala encounter, plus the best of the Great Ocean Road, all in one day.

name: Barossa Valley Behind the Scenes Winery and Vineyard Experience at Kies Family Wines
headings: Nestled in the picturesque Hoffnungsthal Valley, your Barossa Valley luxury helicopter wine experience awaits, offering an exclusive journey through the heart of South Australia’s wine country.

Take in breathtaking views of the beautiful old vines from some of the world’s most famous wine producers and the stunning Barossa Ranges, as you soar above the lush landscapes and vineyards, a unique perspective on this iconic region, before arriving in style at Kies Family Wines for a once-in-a-lifetime experience and a warm welcome, with a guided tour and tasting session, highlighting the best of the Barossa’s winemaking tradition.

The Kies family landed in the German hamlet of Lyndoch in the Barossa Valley, in the 1860’s and have been growing grapes in the region ever since. Enjoy the famous Kies Family Wines hospitality on a tour of their state of the are wine making facility and barrel hall, immersing yourself in the rich history and culture of South Australian wineries and exploring their sustainable and minimal intervention practices.
Allow a member of the Kies Family Wines Team to show you the old Shiraz vines of the Kies estate and run you through their sustainable and minimal intervention practices.

Kies Family Wines built a spectacular state-of-the-art winemaking facility in 2019. Your experience includes a tour of the facility, with an overview of the winemaking process and Barossa Valley history.
Immerse yourself in true Barossa winemaking with a tasting of two wines as you view the French and American Oak barrels used for maturing Kies Family Wines’ premium Barossa Valley Shiraz.
All wines tasted are single-vineyard and Estate-grown, and our wine guide will choose a wine suited to you to pair with your first lunch course, the Barossa Valley Produce Platter.

Settle into the Kies Family Wines Café for your second course and while away the afternoon over lunch with 180° views of the Barossa Ranges. Relish in the local produce and exquisite wines, enhancing your Barossa adventure. Once you are finished your lunch, head into the award winning Kies Family Wines cellar door for a tasting you will not forget – just google Kies Family Wines to get an understanding of what they offer.
After you finish tasting, your helicopter awaits at the Kies Family Wines cellar door to whisk you away for the most incredible views of the Barossa Valley.

headings: A TUSCAN REVERIE OF FRESH PASTAItalian Cook & Dine Experience

Cold outside. Inside? Fresh pasta, bubbling lasagna, golden crostoli, espresso, gelato… and that unmistakable Italian warmth. A Tuscan Reverie of Fresh Pasta is Roving Larder’s hands-on Italian Cook & Dine experience — rustic, generous, comforting, and full of the kind of food that makes winter feel like a very good idea. This is not just a pasta class. It’s a full Italian evening. You’ll roll pasta, fill agnolotti, build a proper lasagna, toss a peppery salad, fry delicate crostoli, and finish with affogato — because Italians understand that dessert should involve both gelato and coffee. You’ll cook. You’ll sip. You’ll learn. Then you’ll sit down at our long table and enjoy the beautiful Tuscan-inspired meal you helped create.

This is the kind of winter night that feels like a little escape to Tuscany. You’ll learn the foundations of fresh pasta, discover how to build flavour into classic Italian dishes, and understand why simple ingredients can become something truly special when treated properly. It’s hands-on, social, generous, and full of heart. Perfect for date nights, catch-ups with friends, birthday gifts, team celebrations, or anyone who believes fresh pasta, lasagna, and a long table are basically therapy.

This is not a cooking demo where you sit politely and watch someone else have all the fun. At Roving Larder, you get involved. Your chef will guide you step by step through the evening’s menu, sharing the techniques, timing, and kitchen tips that make Italian cooking feel approachable and deeply satisfying. You’ll make fresh pasta, prepare fillings and sauces, assemble classic dishes, taste as you go, and enjoy the rhythm of a warm, buzzing kitchen. Then comes the best part. You sit down at the long table to enjoy the meal you’ve helped create — with good company, a drink in hand, and that very satisfying feeling of, “Yes, I made this.”

Please arrive 15 minutes before the class start time so we can welcome you properly. We’ll start with nibbles and a welcome drink while everyone settles in. Your chef will then introduce the menu, explain the flow of the class, and guide the group through the cooking experience. You’ll prepare the dishes, learn the techniques, and enjoy the beautiful chaos of an Italian-inspired kitchen. Once everything is ready, we gather around the table to share the meal together. Good food. Good wine. Good people. A very good winter night.

During this Italian Cook & Dine experience, you’ll learn practical techniques including: Fresh pasta making Learn how to make, roll, and shape fresh pasta dough from scratch. Filling and shaping agnolotti Create delicate pasta parcels filled with creamy ricotta and spinach. Building a traditional lasagna Layer meat ragù, béchamel, and pasta sheets to create the ultimate Italian comfort dish. Making a simple Italian vinaigrette Toss a peppery arugula salad with a light dressing to balance the richness of the meal. Frying crostoli Learn how to make crisp, golden Italian pastries dusted with powdered sugar. Creating affogato Finish with a classic Italian dessert of vanilla gelato “drowned” in hot espresso.

headings: Two training flights in a light aircraft No experience necessary Classroom lesson plus hands-on flying time Feel the exhilaration as you take control and experience not one but two flights from the pilot seat. Record your flights in your own personal pilot log book.

Two training flights in a light aircraft, classroom briefings and a book! The flight lesson commences with a classroom briefing on all you need to know to enable you to control the aircraft on your first lesson. After the briefing the instructor will take you through the pre-flight inspection on your training aircraft before you take your place in the pilot's seat. Your instructor will talk you through the start up, taxiing and take-off before you take to the skies. The first flight is to the west of Launceston airport and lasts approximately 30 minutes. During this time you will be able to have hands on experience in flying the aeroplane. Following the flight there will be opportunity for you to record your flight in your pilot logbook and you will be given an aviation textbook to read prior to your next lesson. For your second flight you will be given a pre-flight briefing on how to fly the aircraft straight and level. Then you will be performing the pre-flight inspection before taking to the sky for a 60 minute lesson. Included in package is 1.5 Hours Dual Flight Instruction, Pilots Log Book and an Introductory Theory Book. Please note: Due to the popularity of this experience, weekend appointments book well in advance. If you have a weekend date in mind please give advance notice.

Allow approx 5 hrs for this package with the first lesson lasting 1.5 hours and the second lesson for 2.5 hours. Available seven days per week during daylight hours. Saturdays and Sundays require five days notice due to availability. How to Get There Tristar Aviation, Launceston Airport, Building 73, Evandale Rd, Western Junction TAS 7212. Detailed directions can be supplied at the time of booking. Please book at least 8 weeks in advance for weekend sessions. Due to the easing of COVID restrictions, experiences will be available again after the 15th of June 2020. Session numbers will be limited and slowly expanded as the situation allows. You're authorised to enter the car park from Gate 4 for Building 73 for your flight experience.
Due to COVID 19 participants are requested to attend alone if possible, if someone needs to accompany them please limit to one person.

You must be of 15 years of age. Flying may be cancelled in certain weather conditions which would make the flight uncomfortable for a novice. Please call the flying school if in any doubt. Any cancelled flights will be rescheduled for a later date. Weight limitation of 90Kg or a max of 190cm applies, if heavier, Please contact the provider directly for alternative arrangements

name: Wild Escapes Tasmania｜Night Safari & Southern Light
headings: "Under the moonlight of Tasmania, illuminate the story of your journey." "Step into the night of Hobart and capture the moment you’ll never want to forget." "Southern stars, nocturnal wildlife, and lantern-lit heritage streets — your exclusive night tour experience in Tasmania, Australia."
Tasmania Aurora Viewing Guide x Wild Night Animal Exploration

Night Sky Tasmania: Tasmania is one of the best locations in Australia to witness the Southern Lights (Aurora Australia). Here is a comprehensive guide to the best viewing spots, optimal viewing times, and essential tips. Animal Exploration: Night creatures come out during the night time!!! Especially for the wild wallabies, and the possums. You have a greater chance to spot them during the starry starry night. Some other animals like Platypus, Ring-tailed possums, Twany frogmouth, Masked Owl...etc. You may also have a chance to spot one of those cute Tasmanian night people.

1. South Bruny Island: Cape Bruny Lighthouse offers an excellent vantage point with minimal light pollution and expansive views. 2. Hobart: Kunanyi / Mount Wellington summit area provides a sweeping view of the southern coastline. 3. Cockle Creek: The southernmost village in Tasmania, offering open, dark skies, making it a prime spot for aurora viewing. 4. Seven Mile Beach: Close to Hobart, a convenient spot for a quick aurora viewing session. 5. South Arm Peninsula: Minimal light pollution and a beautiful southern coastline view.
· The aurora is most active in autumn and winter (May to August). · New moon periods provide the darkest skies for optimal viewing. · Aurora activity peaks when the Kp index reaches 4-5 or higher.

· Aurora Forecast App: Monitor Kp index and cloud cover. · Space Weather Live: Check real-time solar wind data and aurora forecasts. · Facebook Groups: Join Tasmania aurora tracking communities for real-time updates.

Camera Settings: Aperture: f/2.8 or wider ISO: 1600-3200 Exposure Time: 10-20 seconds Use a tripod to prevent camera shake Recommended Gear: Warm clothing, hot drinks Headlamp (with a red light option) Camping chair or blanket

name: 12-Day 4WD Premium Cape York Tour
headings: Your day begins with your [luxury 4WD](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-categories/vehicle) awaiting you at your accommodation in Cairns from 7:45 am to 8:30 am. As we head out of Cairns, you will have a spectacular view over the sugar cane fields, with a stunning backdrop of surrounding Mountains and lush rainforests. Along the journey, you’ll pass Queensland's highest peak: the iconic towering Mount Bartle Frere, while travelling to Lake Barrine teahouse. Marvel at the 500 year old Curtain Fig Tree, the perfect photo opportunity along the way. This is one of the most impressive, gigantic strangler fig trees you will ever see - towering above the canopy at 50m high. The teahouse is a truly beautiful place, located in the Volcanic Crater Lakes National Park, which is within the Wet Tropics World Heritage Area. Lake Barrine boasts an abundance of natural Australian beauty and features a quaint timber heritage tea house perched on the edge of the crystal clear waters of the lake and nestled amongst lush tropical rainforest. Following Lake Barine Teahouse, we make our way through the [Atherton Tablelands](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/atherton-tablelands) and stop off for lunch at [Mungalli Creek Dairy Farm](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/mungalli-biodynamic-cafe). Here you will taste some of the best local biodynamic cheeses Far North Queensland has to offer and enjoy the spectacular rolling hill scenery of the [Atherton Tablelands](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/atherton-tablelands). Our afternoon will be spent visiting magnificent falls that cascade perfectly into a pristine waterhole surrounded by lush Rainforest, it is one of the most photographed Waterfalls in all of Australia - Millaa Millaa. You will check into your [Atherton Tablelands accommodation](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/crater-lakes-rainforest-cottages) for the evening, freshen up, and it will be time to explore on a magical night tour the “#1 Must Do Attraction in Queensland”, the beautiful, [Paronella Park](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/paronella-park). Built in 1937 by Jose Paronella, it is both a living love story and a feat of unique engineering. This is a wonderful photo opportunity and a truly unique experience.

‍We are off to Chillagoe! It’s an early start as we travel through the rolling hills of the [Atherton Tablelands](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/atherton-tablelands) and the iconic “Wheelbarrow Way” stretching from Mareeba to Chillagoe, travelling through farmland, cattle country, wooded savannah and historic towns. Our morning starts with a National Parks Ranger Guided [Chillagoe Cave Tour](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/chillagoe-caves-tour). Delight in the spectacular caverns and passages decorated by stalactites, stalagmites, and flowstones. Their formation began over 400 million years ago, with fluctuating groundwater slowly dissolving and sculpting the caves. Chillagoe was once an ancient Coral Reef that has been transformed into spectacular limestone bluffs with a network of some 560 caves, while early volcanic activity has created rich marble and mineral deposits. Wander the town to see the Railway Station, Bank Vault, Court House, Police Museum, and Post Office. The tall chimney on the edge of the town is part of the former Ore Smelter. Nearby short walking tracks include [Balancing Rock](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/chillagoe-caves-tour) and two Aboriginal Rock Art Galleries. While we are on the edge of Chillagoe town, we will visit Tom Prior’s amazing collection of Ford cars, trucks stored under the galvanized roof of the mechanics shed. This is one of the largest and most geographically remote collections of Ford cars in Australia. There are more than 30 pristine cars and trucks; from a model A to a plastic-protected, red-trimmed white 1970 XW Ford Falcon GT 351c. We will meet with Tom, and marvel at the stories that go with them. ‍Day 3. The Drive to the Daintree Rainforest

Your adventure begins with a visit to the renowned Mareeba Coffee Works, where you'll indulge in the exquisite flavors of locally-produced coffee. Stimulate your senses with a guided tour of the plantation, learning the secrets behind cultivating, roasting, and brewing the perfect cup. Next, venture into the heart of the rainforest to discover the mesmerizing Kuranda Falls. Feel the invigorating spray of the cascading waters and capture stunning photographs surrounded by verdant foliage and soothing sounds of nature. Continue your exploration with a visit to the vibrant Kuranda Markets, a treasure trove of unique arts, crafts, and culinary delights. Immerse yourself in the bustling atmosphere and uncover one-of-a-kind souvenirs, handcrafted by local artisans. The journey continues as you drive down the breathtaking Kuranda Range, a winding route that offers panoramic views of lush rainforest valleys, cascading waterfalls, and the distant Coral Sea. Navigate the hairpin turns and steep inclines, while the awe-inspiring landscape unfolds before your eyes. Your final destination is the secluded [Ferntree Rainforest Lodge](https://ferntreerainforesthotel.com/), an eco-friendly retreat nestled amidst a pristine stretch of UNESCO World Heritage Daintree Rainforest. Unwind in the comfort of your private cabin explore the surrounding nature trails that lead to secluded beaches and panoramic lookouts. Enjoy the pristine pool or savor a delicious meal at the onsite [Cassowary Restaurant](https://www.cassowaryrestaurant.com.au/), boasting stunning ocean views and a menu inspired by local ingredients.

Embark on a half-day adventure with your local guides. Discover wildlife on boardwalks, savor exotic-fruit ice cream, and gain insights into the recent cyclones impact on the area. The afternoon offers you the freedom to explore or partake in various tours available in town. Some tours might need to be booked in advance.
Day 5. Daintree Rainforest to Wolverton Station

Begin your day with an exhilarating journey along the famous 4WD [Bloomfield Track](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/bloomfield-track), heading north bypassing the historic Cooktown. This is a travel based day, so sit back, relax, and enjoy the journey. Weather permitting, embrace the thrill of river crossings en route to your destination - and in many previous departures we have spotted the elusive Cassowary, often accompanied by chicks in this seculded section of the Daintree Rainforest. The day's highlight awaits at the spectacular[ Wujal Wujal Falls](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/bloomfield-falls), where you'll have the chance to stretch your legs and be treated to a interpretive walk, by Far North Escapes. The remainder of the day will be spend venturing along the Peninsula Developmental Road to Wolverton Station "[Wildwishes](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/wild-wishes-at-wolverton-station)" in the Archer River Region. Once you arrive, experience a taste of authentic station life—it's the only station in Far North Queensland with historic cattle droving routes from the 1900s. Settle in for a cozy billy tea and captivating storytelling. Indulge in a truly unique experience as you spend the night at the exclusive[ Wildwishes Glamping Tent](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/wild-wishes-at-wolverton-station), situated at Wolverton Station, Archer River. This is the ultimate glamping destination in[ Cape York](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-categories/cape-york). Day 6. Iron Range National Park

Today’s highlight will be experiencing the[ Iron Range National Park](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/iron-range-national-park) with long sweeping beaches, rocky outcrops, and the largest area of lowland tropical Rainforest in Australia. We will be visiting picturesque Mount Tozer viewing platform in Kutini-Payamu, Iron Range National Park. Be captivated by views from the lookout of colourful heath-clad ranges with Mount Tozer rising impressively in the distance. Learn about the park's cultural and natural history along the way. Cast your eyes over the peaceful heathlands and imagine scenes of violent volcanic activity 250 million years ago! Look for heath plants such as carnivorous pitcher plants and pretty ground orchids. See if you can identify she-oaks with needle-like stems, grevilleas with orange flowers, banksias with papery leaves and woody seed pods, and Jacksonia shrubs with pretty purple-pink flowers. We will also stop to explore the long coastline of stunning[ Quintel Beach](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/iron-range-national-park). The 200 m wide ridged sand flats front the beach, with pretty granite boulders scattered across the sands. Our afternoon arrival brings us to[ The Temple Cape York](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/the-temple-cape-york): off-grid, isolated living at its finest. This is a great location with something for everyone! Fishing addicts, bike enthusiasts, bird watchers, military history buffs, and general lovers of life who want to just soak in the sea views.
Day 7. Choose to relax, undertake activities, or explore Iron Range National Park

Sleep in, or rise early with a sunrise coffee on the deck overlooking Chilli Beach and the Great Barrier Reef — either way, you’re starting the day right. Today is all about slowing down and soaking it all in. Your guides will take you exploring through the stunning Iron Range National Park, with its rich rainforest and chances to spot unique wildlife. Back at The Temple, cool off in the brand new pool, wander the shoreline with sand under your feet, or just let the rhythm of the waves set your pace. It’s the ultimate blend of chill and adventure, all in one serene, off-grid hideaway. In the past, we’d often visit Maʼalpiku — “Restoration Island” — to spend time with the inspiring David Glasheen. Sadly, Resto Dave passed away this year. It was a true privilege to know him, and we miss him dearly.

EXCLUSIVE || November 2019 || SCORE INTERNATIONAL BAJA1000 Pre-Run Tour || Baja Peninsula, Mexico
headings: Exclusive 2019 BAJA1000 Pre-Run Tour, Baja Peninsula, Mexico

Ever wanted to get over to the BAJA1000? We have put together an exclusive 7 Day / 6 Night fully escorted Baja Tour where you Pre-Run the actual BAJA1000 Course for 2019. The Course Map of the 2 full days of pre-running will be a bit of a mystery until the actual course is announced in October 2019, but what we can tell you is that you will have the time of your life. The people of BAJA are the friendliest, the food is to die for and driving the terrain of the most gruelling desert race in the world is truly a BUCKET LIST adventure. So grab some friends, book your spot and join us in Baja. Numbers are limited.  You will be behind the wheel of a $100,000+ purpose-built off-road race car driving at 70 mph over some of the most challenging yet exciting terrain. Suddenly, a ridge is approaching fast and you feel a rush of adrenaline as you hit the throttle and lift off, soaring through the air like a professional BAJA1000 racer. As you revel in the incredible gravity-defying moment, you peer over the front of the open-wheeled buggy to see the ground rapidly approaching. You’re committed now; there’s no time to ponder the landing. For those of us in the racing world, this view of Baja is a common experience, though it never gets old.

11am - Transfer to Ensenada, Baja California, Mexico Meeting Point for Transfer - Terminal 2 by the Lindbergh Statue We will cross the international border 15 minutes south of San Diego for a picturesque drive down the Baja coast. Sweeping vistas of the sparkling blue Pacific Ocean and a quick surfside snack are the prelude to arriving in Ensenada. As you are welcomed by the soaring Mexican flag, enjoy some of the local scenery. This is the Port of Ensenada, where cruise ships bring in tourists by the hundreds. You will get to experience a completely different side of Baja. A brief journey just south of town brings you to the peaceful serenity of our world-famous Estero Beach Resort. Settle into one of the resort’s guest rooms, then find your way into the restaurant at 6:00 for your first official “Driver’s Meeting.” You’ll be greeted by a professional guide and receive important route and safety information. You’ll make the acquaintance of the Baja Challenge cars with a lap around the track at Estero Beach and afterward, you’ll have a chance to socialize with the guides and the rest of the group over dinner. Overnight  - Estero Beach Resort - Ensenada - [http://www.hotelesterobeach.com/en/home.php](http://www.hotelesterobeach.com/en/home.php)

An early wake up will be rewarded with breakfast, hot coffee and orange juice. Once your baggage is loaded into a chase truck, strap yourself in for the first leg of your Baja adventure. With radio communications checked and the 2.5-litre fuel injected engines warmed-up, we’ll head out of Ensenada for the wilds of Baja,traversing on the actual race track with your gps showing you the way any terrain you can think of you will be driving on main roads,silt beds,river crossings,up huge mountains and then alongside the ocean only meters away stopping for lunch and driver changes you wont be able to wipe the smile off your face Overnight - somewhere on the Baja Penisnula enjoying mexican hospitality and talking about all stories of the day long into the night.

A gentle knock on the door awakes you to the crisp, clean air of the Baja countryside. The smell of freshly-ground coffee is a fragrant prelude to the Mexican breakfast waiting in the dining room. With meals complete and bags packed, your guide will lead you into one of the most mind-bending trails in northern Baja. You will take in whats around you more today your used to reading the GPS, know the cars handling better and around every bend there is different terrain to tackle, some of the places we stop at you are bound to rub shoulders with some of the riders and drivers you have seen on TV Overnight  - Mission Santa Isabel - Ensenada enjoying eveyone's stories and sharing a life changing experience together through Mexico

Fully cooked Breakfast After 2 activities for the day you will have a free arvo and night to explore the local atomposphere Ensenada has to offer Exclusive to Aussie Baja Tours - Wed 20th Nov @ 11am (subject to time change) Meet with Roger & Elise Norman, Directors of SCORE INTERNATIONAL where you get a look "behind scenes" of the race and listen to some of the stories from Roger himself, who has won the BAJA1000. Exclusive to Aussie Baja Tours - Wed 20th Nov @ 1pm (subject to time change) Jimmy Spyrs - Operations Manager - PCI - Race Radios and Weatherman Communications. PCI play a very important role in the Baja as communication is key for such a massive race to run smooth and for emergencies to be sorted. Learn why the GPS is vital in knowing where the course goes, dangers, water crossings etc. Overnight - Mission Santa Isabel - Ensenada head out into town for a meal with the locals either grab some street food or dine in a flash Restaurant

Fully cooked Breakfast SCORE INTERNATIONAL BAJA1000 Tech Day - Ensenada Tech Day is a full day where all cars and competitors line up for the technical Inspections for cars and apparel. Once they pass they receive a SCORE sticker and it is race time. You won't know where to look, hundreds of race cars lined up in the main street, live bands, dancers,1000's of spectators, bars, merchandise tents, buritos and coronas, get some autographs from your favourite teams and share some of your stories with them about your pre-running - It is an incredible atmosphere and you'll be in the thick of it all day. At 7pm the drivers briefing will be in held at the Hotel Riviera del Pacífico at the start line in Ensenada, you are welcome to attend with Chris where all the drivers and riders are in the one location. Finish the day off with the Monster Energy Party in the heart of Ensenada, it's PARTY TIME!! Overnight - Mission Santa Isabel - Ensenada

name: 10 Day 4WD Premium Cape York Tour
headings: Your adventure begins with an afternoon pick-up in a [luxury 4WD](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-categories/vehicle) from your Cairns accommodation. Embark on an unforgettable journey from Cairns to the charming Port Douglas and the captivating Cape Tribulation, experiencing the beauty of Australia's tropical paradise through scenic landscapes and thrilling adventures. Take in panoramic views of the Daintree Rainforest, Coral Sea, and Great Barrier Reef from Alexandra Lookout. Check in at the eco-friendly Ferntree Rainforest Lodge and unwind amidst the soothing sounds of the jungle. As the sun sets, stroll along the idyllic Myall Beach for a serene experience. For the ultimate rainforest adventure, join the optional famous Daintree Rainforest Night Walk. Led by expert guides, unveil the hidden secrets of nocturnal creatures in this ancient world. This condensed yet action-packed itinerary will leave you with cherished memories of the unparalleled beauty of Port Douglas to Cape Tribulation. ‍Accommodation: [Ferntree Rainforest Lodge](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/agent-code-pages/ferntree-rainforest-lodge) ‍Meals: Welcome Dinner at [Cassowary Restaurant](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/agent-code-pages/ferntree-rainforest-lodge)

Flop and drop by the stunning lodge pool, or explore where the Great Barrier Reef meets the Daintree Rainforest. In the morning embark on a half-day adventure with your local guides. Discover wildlife on boardwalks, satisfy your sweet tooth at the Daintree Ice Cream Factory and gain insights into the recent cyclones impact on the area. Enjoy a sumptuous lunch at the Cassowary Restaurant, a hidden gem nestled within the vibrant rainforest. The afternoon offers you the freedom to explore or partake in various tours available in town. Some tours might need to be booked in advance. ‍Accommodation: [Ferntree Rainforest Lodge](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/agent-code-pages/ferntree-rainforest-lodge) ‍Meals: Breakfast, lunch and dinner at [Cassowary Restaurant](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/agent-code-pages/ferntree-rainforest-lodge)
Day 3. Daintree Rainforest to Wolverton Station

Begin your day with an exhilarating journey along the famous 4WD [Bloomfield Track](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/bloomfield-track), heading north to the historic Cooktown. Weather permitting, embrace the thrill of river crossings en route to your destination. The day's highlight awaits at the spectacular [Wujal Wujal Falls](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/bloomfield-falls), where you'll be treated to a interpretive walk, by Far North Escapes. Along the way, we'll stop at the iconic [Lions Den Hotel](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/lions-dens-hotel). Established in 1875, its walls are adorned with signatures from around the world—a tradition harking back to the old mining days. Immerse yourself in the hotel's lively atmosphere, often featuring live entertainment. Upon reaching [Cooktown](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/category/cooktown), soak in stunning views before venturing along the Peninsula Developmental Road to Wolverton Station "[Wildwishes](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/wild-wishes-at-wolverton-station)" in the Archer River Region. Here, experience a taste of authentic station life—it's the only station in Far North Queensland with historic cattle droving routes from the 1900s. Settle in for a cozy billy tea and captivating storytelling. Indulge in a truly unique experience as you spend the night at the exclusive[ Wildwishes Glamping Tent](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/wild-wishes-at-wolverton-station), situated at Wolverton Station, Archer River. This is the ultimate glamping destination in [Cape York](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-categories/cape-york). ‍Accommodation: [Wildwishes Glamping Tent](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/wild-wishes-at-wolverton-station) (FNE Exclusive use). Located at [Wolverton Station](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/wild-wishes-at-wolverton-station), Archer River. ‍Meals: Breakfast at [Cassowary Restaurant](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/agent-code-pages/ferntree-rainforest-lodge), Lunch and Dinner catered by Far North Escapes.
Day 4. Wolverton Station to Iron Range National Park

Over the next two days we travel back toward the coastline, experiencing the Lockhart River region. Visiting untouched waterfalls, and the long coastline of stunning[ Chilli Beach](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/iron-range-national-park). We also stop to explore the Lockhart River Art Centre which continues to encourage, work with, promote and represent local artist and their diverse range of artworks through paintings, ceramics, basket weaving and prints. A highlight will be experiencing the [Iron Range National Park](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/iron-range-national-park) with long sweeping beaches, rocky out crops, and the largest area of low land tropical Rainforest in Australia. Our afternoon arrival brings us to [The Temple Cape York](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/the-temple-cape-york): off-grid, isolated living at its finest. This is a great location with something for everyone! Fishing addicts, bike enthusiasts, bird watchers, military history buffs, and general lovers of life who want to just soak in the sea views. ‍Accommodation: [The Temple Cape York](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/the-temple-cape-york) (FNE Exclusive use). Located in Lockhart, just 10 mins from iconic [Chilli Beach](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/iron-range-national-park). ‍Meals: Breakfast, Lunch and Dinner catered by Far North Escapes.
Day 5. Choose to relax, undertake activities, or explore Iron Range National Park

Sleep in, or rise early with a sunrise coffee on the deck overlooking Chilli Beach and the Great Barrier Reef — either way, you’re starting the day right. Today is all about slowing down and soaking it all in. Your guides will take you exploring through the stunning Iron Range National Park, with its rich rainforest and chances to spot unique wildlife. Back at The Temple, cool off in the brand new pool, wander the shoreline with sand under your feet, or just let the rhythm of the waves set your pace. It’s the ultimate blend of chill and adventure, all in one serene, off-grid hideaway. In the past, we’d often visit Maʼalpiku — “Restoration Island” — to spend time with the inspiring David Glasheen. Sadly, Resto Dave passed away this year. It was a true privilege to know him, and we miss him dearly.
Day 6. Iron Range National Park to Bramwell Station

Today we travel wind inland to [Bramwell Station](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/bramwell-station), the most northerly cattle station in Australia. We are treated toa Station Talk followed by live entertainment. Located 2 hours North of Archer River and 4 hours South of the Tip – the station is a well known and well-loved stop for visitors to the Cape over the last 40 years…however it is most famous for its location: the start of the famous 4WD challengethe “[Old Telegraph Line Track](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/old-telegraph-track)”, also known as the “OTL”. ‍Accommodation: [Bramwell Station ‍](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/bramwell-station)Meals: Breakfast, Lunch catered by Far North Escapes, Dinner a Bramwell Buffet
